In Russia, men once had to pay a tax just to keep their beards.
In 1698, Tsar Peter the Great came back from a long trip through Western Europe.
He wanted Russia to look modern. And to him, beards looked old fashioned.
At a welcome party, he grabbed a razor and shaved his nobles himself.
Then he made it law. Shave, or pay.
Rich merchants could pay up to a hundred rubles a year to keep their beards.
And if you paid, you got a beard token, a small coin you had to carry with you.
On it was written: the beard is a useless burden.
And Russia didn't get rid of the beard tax until 1772.
